title: Enhancing On-Device LLM Inference with Historical Cloud-Based LLM Interactions

problem.claim: On-device LLM capabilities lag behind cloud-based LLMs, creating a need to enhance local inference effectively and efficiently.

gap.claim: Using the full datastore improves token-generation quality but causes unacceptably slow generation speed.

contributions.claim: A mobile-device external datastore is built from the user's historical cloud-based LLM interactions and used for nearest-neighbor enhancement.
An optimal datastore subset is selected under a size limit using a submodular optimization objective, with offline and stream-based online selection algorithms.
The offline and online designs are analyzed for performance guarantees and time complexity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluation on three ChatGPT-related dialogue datasets and four on-device LLMs shows significant perplexity improvements while maintaining fast token generation speed.
Smartphone testing reports efficient datastore subset selection in memory usage and computation overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: On-device LLMs support local inference on resource-constrained mobile devices when cloud models are unavailable.
On-device model capabilities lag behind cloud-based models, motivating efficient enhancement.
Historical cloud interactions are stored on the device and used for nearest-neighbor enhancement, while subset selection addresses the cost of the full datastore.
The designs receive theoretical analysis of performance guarantees and time complexity.
Experiments and smartphone overhead tests assess perplexity, generation speed, memory usage, and computation overhead.

source_observation.claim: A historical interaction datastore can enhance on-device LLM inference, but using the full datastore slows generation unacceptably.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval-based enhancement requires explicit control of datastore size and inference cost.

application.claim: Use constrained subset selection when retrieval quality must be balanced against latency and device resources.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach behaves for workloads, devices, models, or datastore limits outside the reported evaluation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the subset-selection algorithms or approximation guarantees.
The abstract does not report dataset sizes, device specifications, baseline models, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the nearest-neighbor representation or datastore construction details.
